posts.content:
A new generation of hardware shouldn’t automatically make the previous one obsolete. ❌

That’s why we design Prusa 3D printers with future upgrades in mind. Your printer can evolve with your business, gain new capabilities over time, and keep delivering value long after the initial purchase. 📈

🛠️ A good example is the Original Prusa MK3. Through successive upgrades, a machine that started as an MK3 can eventually make its way to a CORE One+ (Gen 2). Is taking every single upgrade step always the most cost-effective option? Not necessarily. But the fact that this path exists at all says a lot about how we think about hardware: teach your machines new tricks instead of replacing them just because something newer arrived.

And we’re continuing the same approach with our latest refresh. 🔄 Existing owners can upgrade to the XL+, CORE One L+ and CORE One+ (Gen 2), bringing improvements such as better cooling, cleaner print starts, smoother surfaces, faster preparation and easier maintenance to hardware they already own.

For businesses, that means more than a new feature here and there. It means getting more value from existing equipment, modernizing a print fleet on your own timeline, and extending the useful life of hardware instead of unnecessarily replacing the whole machine. ♻️ Upgrade instead of replace isn’t an afterthought for us. It’s part of how we design our printers.

postedAt.postedAgoText: 2 days ago • Visible to anyone on or off LinkedIn

posts.content:
Refreshing the entire lineup of our 3D printers brought new hardware with the Prusa XL+, CORE One+ (Gen 2) and CORE One L+, but a big part of that progress also happens in firmware. ✨ Recent releases added support for the new Nozzle Wiper, GT1.5 belts and second-generation expansion joints, which significantly shorten the heat-absorption phase on the CORE One+ (Gen 2). On the XL+, firmware also enables the new contactless tool offset calibration: an inductive sensor in the bed measures the position of each nozzle, while thermal expansion compensation accounts for the small change in nozzle length as it heats up. That means more precise alignment between tools without the old calibration pin.
 
Firmware also keeps improving the everyday workflow: more reliable probing and mesh bed leveling, guided calibration order, better filament compatibility checks, an immediate stop when filament runs out, improved material changes, and plenty of fixes under the hood. And these firmware improvements aren't limited to the newest machines - many are also coming to existing Prusa printers.
 
Most tech becomes obsolete over time. Our Prusa 3D printers keep getting better - sometimes through new hardware, but very often through firmware. 🦾

posts.content:
We recently upgraded our printer lineup, and now it's time for the software side. Exactly 15 years after the first Slic3r commit, we’re releasing the public preview of PrusaSlicer 3.0!

We threw out the old UI and rewrote the foundation from scratch for modern multi-tool printing:
• Multi-bed & Multi-project: Mix printers, manage multiple beds, and slice in parallel. 
• Multi-tool Profiles: Designed specifically for multi-nozzle machines like the XL and INDX.
• Safe Plugins: Extend the slicer with custom parametric tools in a secure sandbox. 
• Faster UI: Pin your favorite settings, customize navigation, and enjoy smoother rendering.

And as always: it stays 100% open-source under AGPLv3, complete with a true air-gapped offline mode.

It’s an early preview, so download it, break it, and let us know what you think on GitHub or the forum! (Link in the comments 👇)
Which feature are you testing out first this weekend?

Most people spend the summer vacationing. We were busy… 😅

Say hello to the Prusa XL+, CORE One L+, and CORE One+ (Gen 2)!

If there's one core principle we stick to, it's this: tech shouldn’t become obsolete after a couple of years. That’s why all three refreshed machines have full upgrade paths available for existing owners, and the prices for complete machines stay the same.

• Nozzle wipers standard across all three machines for ultra-clean starts

Most tech gets older. Our 3D printers keep getting better. ✨
That has always been our mindset and it’s how we’ve always approached development. Firmware brings new features, print profiles get fine-tuned, and PrusaSlicer keeps evolving, so your printer can learn new tricks long after it leaves the factory. And when an improvement requires new hardware, the answer shouldn’t be to replace a perfectly good machine. It should be an upgrade.
That’s exactly what the 2026 refreshed lineup is about. The CORE One+ (Gen 2), CORE One L+, and XL+ all come with upgrade paths for current owners. Think of it like upgrading a PC: keep the machine you trust, add a new set of abilities, and keep moving forward. https://lnkd.in/gWsiSSGU
